newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan power capacity to grow 33.1 percent by 2006.
newsitem.headline: Japan power capacity to grow 33.1 percent by 2006.

text.p: The generating capacity of Japan's nine leading power utility companies is expected to rise by about 33.1 percent to 274.4 million kilowatts (kw) by 2006, an industry body said on Monday.
The Federation of Electric Power Companies based the figure on power companies' 10-year programme, which is reviewed annually. The programme was updated recently by the nine power utilities.
The generating capacity of Japan's power utilities is expected to amount to 206.1 million kw at the end of fiscal 1996/97.
The federation said that coal is expected to account for some 15 percent of the generating capacity's power source, up from 10 percent, the fiture projected for 1996.
This represents the largest jump of any energy source.

Liquefied natural gas (LNG) is expected to continue to remain the largest source of power in 2006, accounting for some 25 percent of total generating capacity. That figure is expected to be 24 percent in fiscal 1996/97.
The actual power output in 2006 is expected to reach 1,066.5 billion kilowatt hours (kWh), up from 870.4 billion kWh, the figure projected for fiscal 1996/97.
